title: SoundThinking Announces General Availability of SafetySmart® Field Agent to All ShotSpotter Customers
summary: SoundThinking delivers public safety technology and services — including the ShotSpotter gunshot detection system — that help law enforcement and communities respond faster and save lives.
body_markdown:
*AI-powered assistant helps public safety professionals turn complex operational data into faster insights and better-informed decisions.*


**ORLANDO, Fla., Oct. 23, 2026 --** SoundThinking, Inc. (Nasdaq: SSTI), a leading public safety technology provider, today announced the general availability of SafetySmart® Field Agent to all ShotSpotter agencies, marking the transition from the beta program announced in June to broader commercial availability. SoundThinking is making Field Agent available to ShotSpotter agencies at no additional charge for up to 20 users per agency for the length of their contract term.


Introduced earlier this year with more than 20 beta agencies, Field Agent helps public safety personnel turn operational information into actionable insights without overburdening limited analyst resources. Using natural-language questions, personnel can analyze ShotSpotter data, identify trends, and generate maps, charts, incident summaries and draft briefings. By combining analysis and reporting in a single conversational experience, Field Agent reduces manual tasks and helps personnel across the agency make better-informed operational decisions.


“Field Agent represents a new way for public safety professionals to put ShotSpotter intelligence to work,” said Ralph Clark, President and CEO of SoundThinking. “By making it easier to analyze gunfire activity, uncover patterns and generate actionable insights, we’re helping agencies make faster, better-informed decisions. And as we expand Field Agent to additional sources of operational data, we see even greater opportunities to bring the power of AI into everyday public safety operations.”


The potential applications extend across agency operations. For example, a police chief responding to questions from city leadership could ask Field Agent how gunfire activity has changed over the past month and receive charts and maps highlighting relevant trends. Similarly, a supervisor preparing for an upcoming shift could request a summary of recent gunfire incidents in a specific patrol area, including locations and time-of-day patterns, to help inform operational planning and deployment decisions.


SoundThinking is also developing Feld Agent Skills, a new capability that will allow agencies to create reusable instructions for recurring tasks, such as preparing shift briefings and summarizing incident activity, saving time and improving consistency.


“Field Agent is helping us get more value from information we already have,” said Detective Lucas Roethlisberger, Intelligence Unit / Crime Gun Intelligence Center, St. Louis Metropolitan Police Department. “Instead of waiting for someone to pull data and build an analysis, our team can ask questions directly, identify patterns, and get useful insights much faster. What’s especially exciting is the potential to bring more of our operational data into that experience, giving our people a more complete picture to support better-informed decisions.”


Looking ahead, SoundThinking is expanding the types of information Field Agent can use to support operational decision-making. The company is testing additional agency data sources, including computer-aided dispatch (CAD) and records management system (RMS) information, while enabling agencies to incorporate relevant information through documents and spreadsheets.


SoundThinking is also developing integration with CrimeTracer, its law enforcement search engine, which will extend Field Agent's capabilities to additional investigative and criminal justice information and create opportunities to bring AI-powered decision support to CrimeTracer's extensive network of over 2,100 agencies. Beta availability is planned for November, with general availability targeted for early 2027.


As Field Agent expands across additional agency data sources, responsible AI remains foundational to its design. Human review and decision-making remain central to the workflow: the technology can accelerate searching, synthesis and analysis, but interpretation, validation and operational or investigative decisions remain with authorized personnel.


ShotSpotter agencies can contact their Customer Success Director or email support@soundthinking.com to activate Field Agent access. Attendees at the International Association of Chiefs of Police (IACP) Annual Conference and Exposition in Orlando, Fla., can see a demonstration at Booth 1109 during the exposition, Oct. 25–27, 2026.

**About SoundThinking**


**SoundThinking, Inc. (Nasdaq: SSTI) is a leading public safety technology company that delivers AI- and data-driven solutions for law enforcement, civic leadership, and security professionals. SoundThinking is trusted by approximately 300 customers and supports approximately 2,100 agencies to drive more efficient, effective, and equitable public safety outcomes. The company’s SafetySmart® platform includes ShotSpotter®, the leading acoustic gunshot detection system; CrimeTracer™, the leading law enforcement search engine;**


**SafePointe®, an AI-based weapons detection system; PlateRanger™ (powered by Rekor®), a leading ALPR solution; and Field Agent, an AI layer that transforms public safety data into actionable intelligence. SoundThinking has been designated a Great Place to Work® Company.**
